note: Exported entry points of the NVGate DLLs, extracted from the public C++ headers shipped in the Framework. Each record carries the return type, the typed parameters, the DLL the function belongs to, and the comment found above the declaration in the header. `signature` is the declaration as written, normalised to one line. The `dll` field is taken from the export macro, not guessed. Several functions come in ANSI, UTF-8 and wide-character variants (suffixes `_utf8` and `W`); all are listed because they are distinct entry points.

functions.name: NVGR_LoadFile
functions.description: Load a result file. Load the content of a result file. It is the first function to call previously to access any value of a result file. Once the file is loaded you must check the number of systems by calling the function NVGR_GetNumberOfSystems(). By default a result file contains only one system but if the file has been created by concatenation of several results files, each sources file are saved in a system (i.e. one system by result file). If the file contain more than one system you must select one system by calling the NVGR_SetCurrentSystemNumber() (by default the first system is selected) in order to get the content of the system. Behavior can be adjusted by a previous call to NVGR_SetLoadFileMode(). @see NVGR_GetLoadedFileName and NVGR_GetLoadedFileNameS @see NVGR_SetLoadFileMode @see NVGR_CloseFile @param[in] lpszFileName   Name of the file with the full path and the extension
functions.returns: Returns the file ID (see NVGS_GetCurrentFile, >= 0) if success, -1 otherwise.
functions.signature: EXPORT_API_DLLNVGATERESULTFILE int _stdcall NVGR_LoadFile (const char * lpszFileName);

functions.name: NVGR_SetLoadFileMode
functions.description: Changes the loading strategy of the result file. This changes the way the file is loaded by NVGR_LoadFile. @param[in] mode        0 NVGR_LOAD_FILE_MODE_DEFAULT       All results are loaded in RAM (this the default mode).                                                            This might allocate large amount of memory when result file is large.                        1 NVGR_LOAD_FILE_MODE_SINGLE_RESULT A single result is loaded in RAM. @p resultId specifies the result to load.                                                            This is faster than loading the whole file, and allocate less memory.                        9 NVGR_LOAD_FILE_MODE_NODATA        Same as NVGR_LOAD_FILE_MODE_DEFAULT, except that for some results data points are                                                            not loaded at all. Attempts to access point values will only return zeroes.                                                            Memory usage is moderate, and everything but data points is available.                       10 NVGR_LOAD_FILE_MODE_NODATA_NOCONFIG        Same as NVGR_LOAD_FILE_MODE_NODATA, config data (the tree of setting values) if not loaded.                                                                     Useful to load more quickly, although you cannot access settings (like input labels and such). @param[in] resultId    When mode is 1, this is the resultId of the result to load.                        For the other modes, this parameter is ignored.
functions.signature: EXPORT_API_DLLNVGATERESULTFILE int _stdcall NVGR_SetLoadFileMode(int mode, int resultId);

functions.name: NVGR_GetResultList
functions.description:
Get the list of all the results contained in the file and in the currently selected system. @see NVGR_GetNumberOfResults All parameters are arrays of integers. They must be allocated with a size of NVGR_GetNumberOfResults() integers or more. @param[out] pResultID Array that receives the identifier of the results. Every result in the file has a unique identifier. This identifier will be used in every function that will concern a single result. @param[out] pAnalyzerID Array that receives analyzer identifier associated to the result. Refer to Analyzer identifier for more information @param[out] pResultType Array that receives the type of the result. Refer to Result type for more information @param[out] pChannelID Array that receives the input channel associated to the result. @param[out] pRefChannelID Array that receives the reference channel associated to the result if this result required a reference, otherwise 0. @param[out] pOutputFormat Array that receives the code describing the format of the result. This code is useful only for spectral results. The table below gives the interpretation of the code. @details
-1The result is not of spectral type.
0The result is spectral, defined with real and imaginary part. No operations of weighting, integration or derivation… have been performed on it.
1The result is spectral, defined with module and phase. Operations of weighting, integration or derivation… have been performed on it.
2The result is spectral, defined with real and imaginary part. Operations of weighting, integration or derivation... have been performed on it.
Refer to NVGR_GetOutputOption and NVGR_GetOutputOptionString() for more information on the operations possibly performed on spectral results.
functions.returns: The number of results added in the arrays if successful, otherwise -1.
functions.signature: EXPORT_API_DLLNVGATERESULTFILE int _stdcall NVGR_GetResultList(int* pResultID, int* pAnalyzerID, int* pResultType, int* pChannelID, int* pRefChannelID, int* pOutputFormat);

functions.name: NVGR_GetSource
functions.description: Returns the source of a subanalyzer (submodule). It enables to get information about the input connected to a channel of an analyzer (module) or on the track or the recorder. This method can be called on any sub-analyzer containing a setting "Source" ( Setting = 100 ). For example: - if Input 1 is connected to the Channel 1 of FFT1 :  the source of (10 ,501) is (1,1) - if Input 4 is connected to the Channel 2 of FFT2 :  the source of (11 ,502) is (1,4) - if Input 1 is connected to the Track 1 of the recorder : the source of (3 ,365) is (1,1) - if DC1 1 is connected to the Track 2 of the recorder : the source of (3 ,366) is (1,33) - if Ext synch 1 is connected to the Track 7 of the recorder : the source of (3 ,371) is (1,66) - if Input 1 is connected to the Tacho 1 : the source of (6,731) is (1,1) - if Tacho 1 is connected to the Delta RPM 1 : the source of (5,125) is (6,731) To retrieve the DOF information of the spectrum of the channel 5 of the FFT1: @code NVGR_GetSource(10,505,mmm,sss) @endcode @p mmm is filled with either 1 in online mode (front-end) or 4 in post-analysis (player) @p sss is filled with the input of track number Then, to get the label and component, call @code NVGR_GetStringValue(mmm,sss,1,label) NVGR_GetStringValue(mmm,sss,297,component) @endcode @param[in]  nModule           Module number (analyzer). @param[in]  nSubModule        Submodule number (subanalyzer). @param[out] nSourceModule     Receives the module (analyzer) of the source. @param[out] nSourceSubModule  Receives the submodule (subanalyzer) of the source. @see NVGR_GetResultResponseSubmoduleNumber
functions.signature: EXPORT_API_DLLNVGATERESULTFILE int _stdcall NVGR_GetSource(int nModule, int nSubModule, int* nSourceModule, int* nSourceSubModule);

functions.description: Indicate whether the vector is regular (NVGR_VECTOR_TYPE_REGULAR) or referenced (NVGR_VECTOR_TYPE_REFERENCED). A vector is regular if its X axis values can be expressed as "x[i] = a * i + b", where i is in [0..NVGR_GetResultSize[ Contrary to NVGR_GetVector_1, there is no nReference parameter because all references would be referenced vectors anyway, thus the value of nReference would have no consequence on the result of NVGR_GetVectorType. @param[in]  nResultID    Identifier of a result obtained with NVGR_GetResultList(). @param[out] a_si         The "a" value of the equation, in SI unit (may be NULL if caller is not interested in this value). @param[out] b_si         The "b" value of the equation, in SI unit (may be NULL if caller is not interested in this value). @param[out] a_user       The "a" value of the equation, in user unit (may be NULL if caller is not interested in this value). @param[out] b_user       The "b" value of the equation, in user unit (may be NULL if caller is not interested in this value). functions.name: NVCR_CreateResult
functions.description: Adds a result into a ORXF result file. All results are generated as module number @p NUM_FILE_RESULT_GENERATOR (400). @warning All waterfall results of a given system must have exactly the same @p nWtfDepth and @p dateResult. @param[in] nFileID The FileID returned by a previous call to NVCR_CreateResultFile(). @param[in] nSystemID The SystemID relative to the added result, either 0 or a value previously returned by NVCR_CreateSystem(). @param[in] nProcessType Process type of the added result. @param[in] szProcessCaption Label matching the @p nProcessType. @param[in] szAnalysisCaption Name of the analysis plug in that has generated the data. @param[in] nNumResponse Input channel number for the response. Value in [1..32]. @param[in] szResponseName Label for the response channel. @param[in] nNumReference Input channel number for the reference, if applicable (cross-spectrums, transfer function...). Value in [1..32], or -1 if not specified. @param[in] szReferenceName Label for the reference channel. @param[in] dateResult Acquisition date of the first sample of the result. This is a FILETIME in UTC. For waterfall results, this value MUST be equal to the @p dateResult value provided for waterfall results to other calls to NVCR_CreateResult() and NVCR_AddWtfRefResult() within the same system. @param[in] unWtfDim If result is not a waterfall, use NO_WATERFALL (0). Otherwise: - WATERFALL_2D_SIMPLE_SCALAR (1) for a simple scalar waterfall - WATERFALL_3D (2) for a 3D waterfall - WATERFALL_2D_MULTI_SCALAR_FILE (5) for a scalar waterfall from a group of scalars coming from a file. @param[in] nNumWindow Weighting window. Usually NUM_WIN_UNIFORM (316). @param[in] szXMag Name of the X magnitude. Use "None" or NULL if not applicable. @param[in] szYMagResponse Name of the Y magnitude of the response channel. Use "None" or NULL if not applicable. @param[in] szYMagReference Name of the Y magnitude of the reference channel. Use "None" or NULL if not applicable. @param[in] nWtfDepth Used only with waterfall results. Maximum depth of the waterfall, or -1 for non-waterfall results. MUST be equal to the @p nWtfDepth value provided for waterfall results to other calls to NVCR_CreateResult() and NVCR_AddWtfRefResult() within the same system. @param[in] fAbsPrecisionX Absolute precision in SI for X values, usually 1E-6f. @param[in] fRelPrecisionX Relative precision in SI for X values, usually 1E-6f. @param[in] fAbsPrecisionY Absolute precision in SI for Y values, usually 1E-6f. @param[in] fRelPrecisionY Relative precision in SI for Y values, usually 1E-6f. @param[in] fAbsPrecisionZ Absolute precision in SI for Z values, usually 1E-6f. @param[in] fRelPrecisionZ Relative precision in SI for Z values, usually 1E-6f.
functions.returns: Returns a @p ResultID (value >= 0) or an error (value < 0).
functions.signature: EXPORT_API_DLLNVGATERESULTFILE int _stdcall NVCR_CreateResult( int nFileID , int nSystemID , unsigned int nProcessType , const char * szProcessCaption , const char * szAnalysisCaption , int nNumResponse , const char * szResponseName , int nNumReference , const char * szReferenceName , __int64 dateResult , unsigned int unWtfDim , int nNumWindow , const char * szXMag , const char * szYMagResponse , const char * szYMagReference , int nWtfDepth , float fAbsPrecisionX , float fRelPrecisionX , float fAbsPrecisionY , float fRelPrecisionY , float fAbsPrecisionZ , float fRelPrecisionZ );

functions.name: NVGS_AddChannel
functions.description: Add a channel to the record The type of the channels can be  "osff_Dynamic", "osff_Parametric" or "osff_Trigger". By default, all the channels have 1 and 0 as values for the parameters A and B used to convert samples from user unit to SI unit. Use the NVGS_SetChannelCoeffToSI function to initialize these coefficients if unit conversion is required. Their type is  "Potential_Difference" with unit Volt. The coupling is "AC" and their name is constructed as "Input X". @param[in]  openedMeasurementId		The value returned by NVGS_CreateNewMeasurement @param[in]  type					The channel type @param[in]  samplingRate			The sampling rate of the channel (in samples/s). 									For osff_Dynamic channel type the sampling rate should be a sub multiple of the base sampling rate. 									For osff_Parametric channel type the sampling rate should be 12.5 or 15 spl/s. 									For osff_Trigger channel type the sampling rate should be the base sampling rate. 		-1 : invalid openedMeasurementId 		-2 : measurement deleted or not ready 		-3 : invalid sampling rate 		-4 : unable to create a new record 		-5 : unable to add a new channel
functions.returns: > 0 : returns the new channel index (value to use as parameter in other functions)
functions.signature: EXPORT_API_DLLNVGATERESULTFILE int _stdcall NVGS_AddChannel(OpenedMeasurementId_t openedMeasurementId, OSFFChannelType_t type, float samplingRate);

functions.name: NVGS_CreateNewFile
functions.description:
Create a new signal file. The created signal is composed of @p nNbrTrack tracks with length @p fRecordLength. The new signal can only contain one record. The tracks frequency must be identical. The type of the tracks can be "NVGS_ANALOG_TRACK_TYPE" or "NVGS_SLOW_TRACK_TYPE". By default, all the tracks have 1 and 0 as values for the parameters A and B. Their type is "Potential_Difference" with unit Volt. The coupling is "AC" and their name is constructed as "Input X". The file will be recorded under the filename @p lpszName. @param[in] lpszName The file signal name @param[in] fRecordLength The length of the record, in seconds @param[in] fFrequency Sampling frequency of all the tracks, in Hz. @param[in] nNbrTrack Number of tracks in the signal file @param[in] nType Type for all the tracks: @details
NVGS_ANALOG_TRACK_TYPEANALOG tracks (fast inputs)
NVGS_SLOW_TRACK_TYPESLOW tracks
@deprecated See NVGateSignal.h
functions.signature: EXPORT_API_DLLNVGATERESULTFILE int _stdcall NVGS_CreateNewFile(const char * lpszName , float fRecordLength, float fFrequency , int nNbrTrack , int nType );

functions.name: NVGS_SetTrackFreqCorr
functions.description: Set the frequency correction coefficients for the specified track Possible values for @ nFormat are : CORR_MODULEDB_PHASEDEG        1    -> pfTabCoef must contains the module(in dB)/phase (in degree) correction coefficients and lNbCoef specify the number of couples of complex data CORR_MODULELIN_PHASEDEG        2    -> pfTabCoef must contains the module(in Lin)/phase (in degree) correction coefficients and lNbCoef specify the number of couples of complex data CORR_REALDB_IMAGDB            3    -> pfTabCoef must contains the real(in dB)/imaginary(in dB) correction coefficients and lNbCoef specify the number of couples of complex data CORR_REALIN_IMAGLIN            4    -> pfTabCoef must contains the real(in Lin)/imaginary(in Lin) correction coefficients and lNbCoef specify the number of couples of complex data CORR_INPUT_COEF                5    -> pfTabCoef must contains the correction coefficients for OR3x input version 1 CORR_INPUT_COEF_V2            6    -> pfTabCoef must contains the correction coefficients for OR3x input version 2 CORR_INPUT_COEF_V3            7    -> pfTabCoef must contains the correction coefficients for OR3x input version 3 @param[in] nTrack                    track number, value from 1 to @p nNbrTrack included. @param[in] nFormat                    the format of the coefficients @param[in] fSamplingFrequency        the sampling frequency (in Hz) of the track @param[in] pfTabCoef                pointer on the coefficients array @param[in] lNbCoef                    number of coefficients in the array (in number of complex number if CORR_MODULEDB_PHASEDEG <= nFormat <= CORR_REALIN_IMAGLIN, else in number of float) @deprecated See NVGateSignal.h
functions.signature: EXPORT_API_DLLNVGATERESULTFILE int _stdcall NVGS_SetTrackFreqCorr(int nTrack, short nFormat, float fSamplingFrequency, const float * pfTabCoef, long lNbCoef);
